commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". # NightJar's bug tracker

A small local tracker that stands in for Jira in the course. Issues have keys
like `NJ-12`, a summary, a description, a status and comments.

```bash
make tracker                       # start it (fresh seed issues, new tokens)
cat ~/.nightjar-tracker/tokens.json
export NJ_TRACKER_TOKEN=<read or write token>
python3 tools/tracker/tracker.py search import csv
python3 tools/tracker/tracker.py get NJ-12
```

- **Two tokens.** The read token can search and read. Only the write token can
  create issues or add comments (the server answers 403 otherwise).
- **Search** returns issues whose summary or description contain every word
  you give (a word matches the start of a word, so `import` finds `imported`).
- **Data** lives in `~/.nightjar-tracker/`, outside the repository.

"""Command-line client for NightJar's local bug tracker (a stand-in for Jira).

    python3 tools/tracker/tracker.py search WORDS...       # issues containing every word
    python3 tools/tracker/tracker.py get NJ-12
    python3 tools/tracker/tracker.py create --draft bug-drafts/x.md
    python3 tools/tracker/tracker.py comment NJ-12 --draft bug-drafts/x-comment.md

Reads the address from NJ_TRACKER_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8765) and the
token from NJ_TRACKER_TOKEN. A draft is a Markdown file whose first line is
"# <summary>"; the rest is the description. Every search is logged to
.tracker/searches.jsonl.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlencode

URL = os.environ.get("NJ_TRACKER_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765")


def call(method: str, path: str, body: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    token = os.environ.get("NJ_TRACKER_TOKEN", "")
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        URL + path,
        method=method,
        data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None,
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=10) as response:
            return json.loads(response.read())
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        sys.exit(f"tracker: {error.code} {json.loads(error.read()).get('error')}")
    except urllib.error.URLError as error:
        sys.exit(f"tracker: can't reach {URL} ({error.reason}). Is `make tracker` running?")


def read_draft(path: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    lines = Path(path).read_text().splitlines()
    if not lines or not lines[0].startswith("# "):
        sys.exit(f"tracker: {path} must start with '# <summary>'")
    return lines[0][2:].strip(), "\n".join(lines[1:]).strip()


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser("search", help="issues containing every word")
    p.add_argument("words", nargs="+")
    p = sub.add_parser("get", help="one issue with its description and comments")
    p.add_argument("key")
    p = sub.add_parser("create", help="file a new bug from a draft")
    p.add_argument("--draft", required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser("comment", help="add a draft as a comment on an issue")
    p.add_argument("key")
    p.add_argument("--draft", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.command == "search":
        query = " ".join(args.words)
        result = call("GET", "/rest/api/2/search?" + urlencode({"text": query}))
        log = Path(".tracker/searches.jsonl")
        log.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        with log.open("a") as f:
            f.write(
                json.dumps({"time": time.time(), "query": query, "hits": result["total"]}) + "\n"
            )
        print(f"{result['total']} issue(s) contain: {query}")
        for issue in result["issues"]:
            print(f"  {issue['key']}  {issue['status']:<6}  {issue['summary']}")
    elif args.command == "get":
        issue = call("GET", f"/rest/api/2/issue/{args.key}")
        print(f"{issue['key']}  {issue['status']}  {issue['summary']}\n\n{issue['description']}")
        for n, comment in enumerate(issue["comments"], 1):
            print(f"\n--- comment {n}\n{comment}")
    elif args.command == "create":
        summary, description = read_draft(args.draft)
        result = call("POST", "/rest/api/2/issue", {"summary": summary, "description": description})
        print(f"Created {result['key']}: {summary}")
    elif args.command == "comment":
        summary, description = read_draft(args.draft)
        body = {"body": f"{summary}\n\n{description}"}
        call("POST", f"/rest/api/2/issue/{args.key}/comment", body)
        print(f"Commented on {args.key}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1	"""Sleep diary storage (SQLite) and CSV import.
2	
3	Datetimes are stored in UTC (ISO 8601) so they sort correctly; each night keeps
4	the IANA time zone the user was in, so local times can always be rebuilt.
5	"""
6	
7	import csv
8	import io
9	import sqlite3
10	from collections.abc import Iterator
11	from contextlib import contextmanager
12	from datetime import UTC, datetime, time
13	from pathlib import Path
14	
15	from nightjar.models import Night, User, zone
16	
17	DEFAULT_USER = User(
18	    name="Sam", timezone="America/Toronto", quiet_start=time(23, 0), quiet_end=time(7, 0)
19	)
20	CSV_COLUMNS = {"bedtime", "wake_time", "timezone", "notes"}
21	
22	SCHEMA = """
23	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS nights (
24	    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
25	    bedtime_utc TEXT NOT NULL,
26	    wake_time_utc TEXT NOT NULL,
27	    timezone TEXT NOT NULL,
28	    notes TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
29	);
30	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_settings (
31	    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id = 1),
32	    name TEXT NOT NULL,
33	    timezone TEXT NOT NULL,
34	    quiet_start TEXT,
35	    quiet_end TEXT
36	);
37	"""
38	
39	
40	class Diary:
41	    """All reads and writes for one user's diary."""
42	
43	    def __init__(self, path: str | Path) -> None:
44	        self.path = str(path)
45	        with self._connect() as db:
46	            db.executescript(SCHEMA)
47	
48	    @contextmanager
49	    def _connect(self) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
50	        db = sqlite3.connect(self.path)
51	        try:
52	            with db:  # commits on success, rolls back on error
53	                yield db
54	        finally:
55	            db.close()
56	
57	    def add_night(self, night: Night) -> None:
58	        with self._connect() as db:
59	            db.execute(
60	                "INSERT INTO nights (bedtime_utc, wake_time_utc, timezone, notes)"
61	                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
62	                (
63	                    _to_utc_text(night.bedtime),
64	                    _to_utc_text(night.wake_time),
65	                    night.timezone,
66	                    night.notes,
67	                ),
68	            )
69	
70	    def add_nights(self, nights: list[Night]) -> int:
71	        for night in nights:
72	            self.add_night(night)
73	        return len(nights)
74	
75	    def nights(self) -> list[Night]:
76	        """All nights, newest first."""
77	        with self._connect() as db:
78	            rows = db.execute(
79	                "SELECT id, bedtime_utc, wake_time_utc, timezone, notes"
80	                " FROM nights ORDER BY bedtime_utc DESC"
81	            ).fetchall()
82	        return [
83	            Night(
84	                id=row[0],
85	                bedtime=datetime.fromisoformat(row[1]),
86	                wake_time=datetime.fromisoformat(row[2]),
87	                timezone=row[3],
88	                notes=row[4],
89	            )
90	            for row in rows
91	        ]
92	
93	    def user(self) -> User:
94	        with self._connect() as db:
95	            row = db.execute(
96	                "SELECT name, timezone, quiet_start, quiet_end FROM user_settings"
97	            ).fetchone()
98	        if row is None:
99	            return DEFAULT_USER
100	        return User(
101	            name=row[0],
102	            timezone=row[1],
103	            quiet_start=_parse_time(row[2]),
104	            quiet_end=_parse_time(row[3]),
105	        )
106	
107	    def save_user(self, user: User) -> None:
108	        zone(user.timezone)  # validate before saving
109	        with self._connect() as db:
110	            db.execute(
111	                "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO user_settings VALUES (1, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
112	                (
113	                    user.name,
114	                    user.timezone,
115	                    _format_time(user.quiet_start),
116	                    _format_time(user.quiet_end),
117	                ),
118	            )
119	
120	
121	def parse_csv(text: str) -> list[Night]:
122	    """Parse diary CSV: bedtime,wake_time,timezone,notes (ISO 8601 with UTC offsets)."""
123	    reader = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text))
124	    missing = CSV_COLUMNS - set(reader.fieldnames or [])
125	    if missing:
126	        raise ValueError(f"CSV is missing columns: {', '.join(sorted(missing))}")
127	    nights = []
128	    for line_number, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):
129	        try:
130	            nights.append(
131	                Night(
132	                    bedtime=parse_aware(row["bedtime"]),
133	                    wake_time=parse_aware(row["wake_time"]),
134	                    timezone=row["timezone"].strip(),
135	                    notes=(row["notes"] or "").strip(),
136	                )
137	            )
138	        except ValueError as error:
139	            raise ValueError(f"Line {line_number}: {error}") from error
140	    return nights
141	
142	
143	def parse_aware(text: str) -> datetime:
144	    """Parse an ISO 8601 datetime that must include a UTC offset."""
145	    value = datetime.fromisoformat(text.strip())
146	    if value.tzinfo is None:
147	        raise ValueError(f"{text!r} has no UTC offset")
148	    return value
149	
150	
151	def local_input_to_aware(text: str, timezone: str) -> datetime:
152	    """Turn an HTML datetime-local value ('2026-03-19T23:00') into an aware datetime."""
153	    return datetime.fromisoformat(text).replace(tzinfo=zone(timezone))
154	
155	
156	def _to_utc_text(value: datetime) -> str:
157	    return value.astimezone(UTC).isoformat()
158	
159	
160	def _parse_time(text: str | None) -> time | None:
161	    return time.fromisoformat(text) if text else None
162	
163	
164	def _format_time(value: time | None) -> str | None:
165	    return value.strftime("%H:%M") if value else None
